title: Dependency floor is bootstrap availability, not acceptance
summary: Dependency-floor seeding establishes exact package trees needed so later plans can resolve. It preserves existing package trees, adds missing trees and writes a bootstrap ledger; it never converts mere availability into acceptance.
invariants: BOOTSTRAP_ONLY_NOT_ACCEPTANCE is a semantic boundary, not wording.
Existing accepted package directories are preserved rather than overwritten.
A floor is consumed by the planner; it is not proof that dependencies have passed fresh qualification.
Repository catalogue identity is manifest-first even when the floor was seeded from bundle layout.

provenance.claim: Independent acceptance records dependency-floor seed counts and BOOTSTRAP_ONLY_NOT_ACCEPTANCE.
Seeder creates package trees and bootstrap ledger through main transaction.
